# Can I run GTA?

> Checks PC specs against the minimum and recommended requirements of every PC Grand Theft Auto release (GTA III to GTA V Enhanced, plus projected GTA VI). Free JSON API, no key, CORS open.

Guidance for AI agents:

- Pass every spec the user gave. Ask for missing ones instead of guessing; omitted specs give `unknown`, never a pass.
- Use exact marketing names for hardware (`Core i5-12400F`, `GeForce RTX 3060`, `Radeon RX 6600 XT`). If a name is not recognised, `suggestions` lists the closest known names; confirm with the user which one they have, then retry.
- GTA VI has no official PC requirements. Its figures are third-party projections (`confidence: approximate`); say so when reporting.
- Give the user `resultsUrl` from the response so they can see the same check on the site.

## Check a PC

GET https://canirungta.com/api/check

Query parameters (at least one of cpu, gpu, ram, vram, disk is required):

- cpu: CPU model, e.g. `Ryzen 5 5600`
- gpu: GPU model, e.g. `RTX 3060`
- ram: system RAM in GB, e.g. `16`
- vram: GPU memory in GB, e.g. `12` (only used together with gpu)
- disk: free disk space in GB, e.g. `200`
- os: `windows` (default), `linux`, `macos` or `mobile`
- windows: Windows major version; pass `10` for Windows 10 and 11. If omitted, the OS check is `unknown` for games that need Windows 10
- version: comma-separated version ids to limit the results (default: all)

Version ids: `gta-vi`, `gta-v-enhanced`, `gta-v-2015`, `gta-iv-complete`, `gta-iv-original`, `gta-sa-definitive`, `gta-sa-original`, `gta-vc-definitive`, `gta-vc-original`, `gta-iii-definitive`, `gta-iii-original`

Example:

https://canirungta.com/api/check?cpu=Ryzen%205%205600&gpu=RTX%203060&ram=16&vram=12&disk=200&os=windows&windows=10&version=gta-v-enhanced,gta-vi

Response (JSON):

- `input`: the specs as parsed
- `errors`: invalid inputs that were skipped (the check still runs on the rest)
- `warnings`: CPU/GPU names that were not recognised
- `suggestions`: `{ cpu: [], gpu: [] }`, up to 3 closest recognised names for each unrecognised one (empty when nothing is close)
- `resultsUrl`: the website pre-filled with the same specs
- `results`: one entry per version with `id`, `title`, `edition`, `verdict`, `summary` (one sentence), `confidence`, `sourceUrl` and `checks`
- `checks`: per component (CPU, GPU, RAM, VRAM, Disk, OS) with `status` (`pass`/`fail`/`unknown`), `actual`, `required` (the minimum) and `note`

Verdicts: `runs-well` (meets recommended), `runs` (meets minimum only), `cannot` (fails a minimum), `unknown` (missing or unrecognised specs; supply more), `needs-windows` (nothing failed, but a non-Windows OS needs Proton/Wine), `unsupported` (mobile).

A request with no specs returns HTTP 400 with an `error` message.

## Requirements data

- Markdown, all versions on one page: https://canirungta.com/requirements.md
- JSON: https://canirungta.com/api/versions.json, with the minimum/recommended specs per version, source URLs and a `confidence` field (`official`, `approximate`, `unannounced`). `null` means no published figure.

## Link a user to their results

https://canirungta.com/?cpu=Ryzen%205%205600&gpu=RTX%203060&ram=16&vram=12&disk=200

The page accepts the same cpu, gpu, ram, vram and disk parameters and shows the verdicts for them. The OS is read from the visitor's browser.

## Other interfaces

- OpenAPI 3.1 spec: https://canirungta.com/openapi.json (import as a GPT Action or any tool-calling client)
- MCP server (streamable HTTP, stateless, no auth): https://canirungta.com/mcp
  - `check_gta_compatibility`: same parameters as /api/check
  - `list_gta_requirements`: the requirements data, optional `version` filter
- Discovery: https://canirungta.com/.well-known/mcp.json
- Browser agents: the page registers `check_gta_compatibility` through WebMCP (`navigator.modelContext`) where the browser supports it; otherwise open "Get exact results" and fill the "Enter your PC specs" form.
